answer: One defence is a staking ledge: every agent must lock a deposit of real value before it can trade, and the deposit is slashed when peers prove fraud. A newcomer starts with a thin, quartz-like reputation that only thickens after verified work, so a Sybil operator who spawns thousands of identities pays the stake thousands of times while an honest agent pays once. A violet flag marks accounts whose behaviour diverges from their claimed history, letting the market price suspicion before any trade clears.
